questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why people in Britain prefer bread to rice
The different types of rice around the world
The importance of rice and a new way to grow it with less water
How to cook rice without wasting water
questions.why: They discuss rice as a staple food and a new technique helping farmers grow it in a changing climate.

questions.q: What kind of food does Neil often eat?
options: Basic filling food like bread and potatoes
Mostly rice dishes
Lots of fresh fruit and vegetables from the market
Mainly meat and fish
questions.why: Neil says he eats basic things that fill him up, like bread and potatoes.

questions.q: Why is growing rice becoming a problem?
options: Fewer people want to eat it
It needs lots of water, and climate change brings droughts and floods
Farmers are moving to cities
It is too expensive to sell because farmers have to pay so much for land
questions.why: Neil says rice is a 'thirsty' crop, and droughts and flooding caused by climate change are a problem.

questions.q: According to Dr Yvonne Pinto, how many people rely on rice as their main food?
options: About one billion
About two billion
Almost everyone in the world
About four billion
questions.why: She says 50 to 56 percent of the world, 'roughly about four billion people', rely on rice.

questions.q: Where does Dr Pinto say the demand for rice is increasing?
options: Only in South Asia and Southeast Asia
In North America
In Australia
In continents like Africa
questions.why: She says 'increasingly the appetite for it is growing in continents like Africa'.

questions.q: How does the AWD technique work?
options: Fields are flooded all the time
Pipes show water levels, so farmers need fewer flooding cycles
Rice is grown indoors without soil
Farmers plant a new variety of rice every month to see which grows best
questions.why: Pipes placed 15cm underground show water levels, reducing flooding cycles from 25 to 20.

questions.q: According to Jean-Philippe Laborde, why was it hard to persuade farmers to try AWD?
options: They were afraid of losing money
They didn't have enough water
They didn't trust foreign companies
The pipes were too expensive
questions.why: He says the main challenge was farmers' 'apprehension to lose revenues'.

questions.q: What were the results of using AWD?
options: More water was used than before, but farmers grew much more rice
Methane went up, but costs went down
Less water, electricity and methane, and more rice
The rice tasted better, but there was less of it
questions.why: Beth says water, electricity and methane decreased, and the amount of rice increased.
